Electron renderer windows (main and widgets) with sandbox: false and a shared preload exposing the Electron toolkit API

rationale: The answer identifies the desktop platform correctly as Electron (stage-tamagotchi) from multiple implementation signals and never treats the legacy Tauri layer (AGENTS.md still mentions crates/, but no crates/ directory exists in this checkout) as current. Every load-bearing claim was verified against implementation: the DI composition root and parallel emitAppBeforeQuit/injeca.stop shutdown (main/index.ts), reusable/referenced window managers with the setMaxListeners(0) window-namespaced-context TODO, the in-process ExtensionHost({runtime:'electron'}) -> FileSystemLoader import(entrypoint), the iframe sandbox token string (verified in both extension-ui-host.vue and gamelet kit), the cookie/session-authorized static asset route, server-runtime's auth/module-registration/health/heartbeat/routing and server-sdk's token/announce/heartbeat/reconnect, the local-only+remote-observable (no remote-callable) expose policies of gameletKit and toolKit, the node runtime's unimplemented transports, the disabled!=unload behavior in setEnabled, sandbox:false on main and widgets windows, and the McpStdioManager process lifecycle. The review clearly separates current evidence from future intent, explains where change spreads (composition root, global ipcMain listeners, privileged preload reuse), compares three viable options including the current shape with explicit quality-attribute/cost/risk/rollback trade-offs, grounds its hybrid recommendation in verified evidence, and gives a five-phase migration whose acceptance criteria are concrete, observable, and reversible. Project-specific facts stay anchored to the repo rather than being smuggled into universal rules. No factual errors, no decision-relevant documentation/implementation conflicts.
